rules.summary: The Seminole County School Board says it recognizes the right of high school athletes to use and benefit from their name, image and likeness. It says athletes must still follow Florida law, State Board of Education rules, Board policies and FHSAA bylaws.
rules.conditions: The policy is one paragraph. It sets no district process, form, contact or approval step. The detail comes from FHSAA rules.
rules.short_answer: Yes. The district recognizes NIL, within FHSAA and Board rules.

sources.quote: The School Board recognizes the rights of high school student-athletes to use and benefit from their name, image, and likeness (NIL) in various activities.
Likewise, student athletes must comply with all applicable bylaws of the Florida High School Athletics Association (FHSAA).

rules.summary: The Seminole County School Board says that failing to follow these laws, rules and regulations may affect an athlete's amateur status.
rules.short_answer: Breaking the rules can put amateur status at risk.

sources.quote: Failure to adhere to any of these laws, rules, and/or regulations may, among other things, impact the amateur status of a student athlete.
